publicationTitle: 2024 2nd China Power Supply Society Electromagnetic Compatibility Conference (CPEMC)
abstract: Based on the circuit structure and working principle of DC/DC switching power supply, this paper analyzes its electromagnetic interference mechanism from the perspective of EMC three elements, including electromagnetic interference source and interference propagation path. Then, considering the fact that the DC/DC switching power supply module usually works in a combined state and it is difficult to obtain internal detailed information, a method of extracting key information by means of test and other methods is proposed, and a simulation model of the DC/DC switching power supply module is established according to the circuit topology structure, so as to realize the modeling and simulation analysis of the switching power supply board.

articleTitle: Analysis of Aircraft Surface Charge Distribution Based on BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd China Power Supply Society Electromagnetic Compatibility Conference (CPEMC)
abstract: When aircraft fly at high altitudes, charges accumulate on the surface of the aircraft due to collision and friction with particles in the air, jeopardizing flight safety. In this study, we propose an inversion analysis model established through the neural network method, which uses the curvature of the aircraft surface as input to invert the charge distribution on the aircraft surface. Firstly, the characteristics of charge distribution on the aircraft surface are obtained through simulation calculations, and these data are used for training and testing of the neural network. Then, a BP neural network model is built and trained using MATLAB. The root mean square error (RMSE) of the inverse results of the trained neural network is 0.036, and the average absolute error (MAE) is 0.022. Finally, a scaled-down aircraft model is established for ground experimental verification. The results demonstrate the feasibility of conducting inverse analysis of aircraft surface charge distribution through the construction of a neural network. This method can provide reference input for the analysis of aircraft electrostatic safety.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Interrelationships of VFTO, TEV, and EMF in Ultra-High Voltage Substations
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd China Power Supply Society Electromagnetic Compatibility Conference (CPEMC)
abstract: The interrelationship between very fast transient over-voltage (VFTO), transient enclosure voltage (TEV), and electromagnetic fields (EMF) is crucial for understanding the formation mechanism of switching transients in Gas Insulated Substations (GIS). First, this paper qualitatively analyzes the formation mechanisms of EMF and TEV, arguing that the EMF is composed of the incident field of GIS bushing current and the scattering field of induced current on the GIS enclosure, while TEV is formed by the induced current flowing through the enclosure’s surface impedance. This analysis leads to inferences regarding the amplitude and frequency relationships between VFTO, TEV, and EMF. Then, based on the 1000kV GIS circuit at the Wuhan UHV AC Test Base, switch operation tests were conducted, and the waveforms of VFTO, TEV, and EMF were synchronously measured. The measurement results verified the rationality of the proposed inferences.

articleTitle: Modeling of Common-mode EMI from an All-in-one Motor Drive Module of Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd China Power Supply Society Electromagnetic Compatibility Conference (CPEMC)
abstract: All-in-one motor drive module is the core component of electric vehicle. The internal space of the all-in-one motor drive module is compact, and the common-mode (CM) electromagnetic interference (EMI) coupling mechanism is complex, which seriously deteriorates the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) performance of the system. Therefore, it is of great significance to accurately predict the CM EMI in the all-in-one motor drive module for evaluating the EMC performance of the system. Due to the complex structure of the all-in-one motor drive module, there is also a lack of relevant research in EMI modeling. In particular, it is difficult to extract the parasitic capacitance parameters of insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) module and construct a high-frequency model of multi-port bus capacitor. In view of this situation, this paper presents the extraction method of IGBT module parameters and the high-frequency model of bus capacitor. Moreover, the vector matching method is used to construct the interference model of motor and EMI filter. The high-frequency parasitic parameters of the cable are extracted. Based on these analyses, we construct a CM EMI overall model of all-in-one motor drive module. The all-in-one motor drive module EMI model is verified by simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Design of a Chaotic Carrier Frequency Modulation Switched-Mode Power Supply Controller Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd China Power Supply Society Electromagnetic Compatibility Conference (CPEMC)
abstract: An FPGA-based controller that employs Chaotic Digital Pulse Width Modulation(CDPWM) is proposed to suppress electromagnetic interference (EMI) in Switched-Mode Power Supplies (SMPS). Utilizing the Tent map to generate a chaotic sequence, the proposed system modulates the switching frequency, resulting in a more uniform energy spectrum and reduced EMI. The effectiveness of the CCFM technique is validated through theoretical analysis and experimental results, which show significant EMI reduction. The study demonstrates the potential of digital chaotic frequency modulation in enhancing the performance and regulatory compliance of SMPS.

articleTitle: Research on the Transformer Lightweight Technology of Isolated Bidirectional DC/DC Converter for Aerospace
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd China Power Supply Society Electromagnetic Compatibility Conference (CPEMC)
abstract: The isolated bidirectional DC/DC converter serves as the main body of the aerospace servo power supply, and the design of its transformer volume and weight is the key to optimization. In this paper, aiming at the magnetic integration scheme of the CLLLC resonant converter, a coupled integrated structure with interleaved winding placement is adopted, and a mathematical model of the excitation inductance, leakage inductance and air gap magnetic resistance is established. The key influencing factors of the leakage inductance are pointed out, and four design criteria for the integrated transformer are proposed. With the weight optimization of the power converter as the research target, it is clarified that different turn combinations are the key factors affecting the weight of the integrated transformer. An optimized design scheme for the integrated transformer is given under the condition that the total loss and performance remain unchanged. Compared with the discrete transformer, the total weight and volume of the final integrated transformer are greatly reduced. Finally, the correctness and feasibility of the theoretical analysis are verified through a 7.6kW prototype.

articleTitle: A Failure Risk Assessment Method of Secondary System in Lightning Electromagnetic Pulse Environment of Island Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd China Power Supply Society Electromagnetic Compatibility Conference (CPEMC)
abstract: The natural environment of an island microgrid is harsh and complex, rendering the secondary system susceptible to lightning electromagnetic interference, thereby resulting in system failure. An island microgrid’s lightning electromagnetic pulse environment is the focus of this paper, which offers a method to evaluate the potential for secondary system failure. The effectiveness and practicability of the evaluation method are verified by a case study. Proposed is a functional failure probability evaluation model, based on a function diagram, to illustrate the repercussions of lightning electromagnetic pulses on the secondary system. Additionally, the reliability block diagram-based evaluation method is extended so that direct calculation of function failure probability can be achieved according to the function diagram. Finally, an example involving data acquisition functionality within the secondary system of an island microgrid is utilized to illustrate how this evaluation method can be applied in practice. The proposed method offers intuitive simplicity with minimal error and excellent generality, making it suitable for evaluating both safety and stability aspects pertaining to island microgrid’s secondary systems operating under unique environmental conditions.
